title: Dawn landing, hanok lanes, silver-grass sunset
summary: Taxi straight to a room that is already yours (booked from Oct 16), sleep until lunch, then an easy hanok-lane stroll and the opening evening of the Seoul Eulalia Festival. Hongdae's Saturday-night buzz is there if anyone still has energy.
autumn_note: Opening day of the 25th Seoul Eulalia (silver grass) Festival at Haneul Park, 10:00-21:00 with evening lighting; the plumes are at peak. Sunset ~17:55.

items.title: Land at Incheon T1, immigration and bags
items.detail: File the free e-Arrival Card online in the 3 days before (US citizens are K-ETA-exempt through 2026). Buy a T-money or WOWPASS card at a convenience store for subways later.

items.title: Taxi to the Jongno hotel
items.detail: Regular taxi from the rank, ~70-80k KRW per car with tolls. Dawn traffic is light, about an hour door to door.

items.title: Check in (Oct 16 night booked) and sleep
items.detail: Because the room is booked from the night of Oct 16 it is ready on arrival: shower, breakfast (included at 4rest Stay), then a proper nap. This is what makes the rest of the day work.

items.title: Ikseon-dong hanok alleys + lunch
items.detail: A tight warren of 1920s urban hanok turned into cafes and dumpling shops, 5 minutes from the hotel. Small-scale, Kamakura-Komachi-dori energy.
items.tip: Weekend lunchtime queues are real; if Changhwadang has a line, any cafe courtyard works.

items.title: Bukchon lanes and Samcheong-dong
items.detail: Walk up through Gahoe-dong's tiled-roof lanes for the view toward Namsan, then down Samcheong-dong's cafe street. Keep voices low: people live here.
items.tip: The red zone (Bukchon-ro 11-gil) is open to visitors only 10:00-17:00, with fines up to 100,000 KRW outside those hours.

items.title: Haneul Park silver-grass festival at sunset
items.detail: Taxi ~30 min (~20k per car) to World Cup Park, ride the Maengkkongi cart or climb the 291 Haneul stairs, and walk the hilltop sea of silver plumes as the sun drops over the Han River. Stay for the evening lighting after ~18:15.
items.cost_note: cart one way (unconfirmed 2026 fare); free on foot
items.tip: Saturday afternoon is the busiest slot of the festival week; the crowd thins after dark.

items.title: Mangwon Market dinner, optional Hongdae
items.detail: 10 min by taxi down the hill: graze Mangwon Market's fried chicken, kalguksu and hotteok stalls. If jet lag allows, it is 10 more minutes to Hongdae's Saturday-night busking on Eoulmadang-ro, the closest thing to Shibuya crossing energy. Taxi back to Jongno ~25 min.

food.name: Changhwadang (Ikseon-dong)
food.note: Hand-made dumplings and tteokbokki in a hanok; the easy first Korean meal. Walk-in.

food.name: Mangwon Market stalls
food.note: Dakgangjeong (crispy glazed chicken), kalguksu and croquettes; stalls run to about 21:00, some close earlier.

rainy_swap: Swap Haneul Park for the National Museum of Korea (free, open to 21:00 on Saturdays, 'Our Dining Table' special exhibition to Oct 25), then dinner in Ikseon-dong.

title: Secret Garden by day, palace pond by night
summary: The royal Secret Garden tour in the morning, Insadong and Jogyesa at an easy pace, an afternoon rest, then Gwangjang Market and the lantern-lit pond show at Changgyeonggung. Sunday is the right day: Changdeokgung and Changgyeonggung are closed Monday.
autumn_note: Huwon's maples are just starting (peak is late Oct-early Nov); Changgyeonggung's Chundangji pond is one of the better palace foliage spots.

items.title: Changdeokgung + Huwon (Secret Garden) tour
items.detail: Walk the UNESCO palace (Injeongjeon, Nakseonjae), then the ~90-min guided tour through the wooded rear garden to Buyongji pond and the Ongnyucheon stream, the closest Seoul gets to a Kamakura temple garden.
items.booking: Huwon tickets release online 6 days ahead at 10:00 KST: for Oct 18 that is Mon Oct 12 10:00 KST = Sun Oct 11 21:00 in Newark. Pick an English or Korean slot around 10:30-11:30. Limited on-site tickets exist but sell out on autumn Sundays.
items.tip: The palace is 10 min on foot from 4rest Stay.

items.title: Insadong + Jogyesa temple
items.detail: Lunch on Insadong-gil, browse the craft shops and Ssamziegil, then step into Jogyesa, the working head temple of Korean Zen under 500-year-old trees.
items.tip: Jogyesa's chrysanthemum display usually starts mid-late October.

items.title: Hotel break
items.detail: Day 2 of jet lag: nap now so the evening works.

items.title: Gwangjang Market food alley
items.detail: The 1905 covered market: mung-bean bindaetteok fried to order, beef yukhoe, mayak gimbap and makgeolli at the counters. Food stalls are open on Sundays even though fabric shops close.
items.tip: Prices are posted since the 2023-24 overcharging scandals; check before ordering.

items.title: Changgyeonggung 'Mulbit Yeonhwa' night show
items.detail: Short taxi north. The palace stays open to 21:00; the media-art pond show runs at 19:00, 19:30 and 20:00 (~16 min) and the 1909 glass botanical house is lit.
items.booking: Ticketlink or Creatrip (foreigners), 1,000 KRW including admission; book a 19:30 slot now.

items.title: Jongno 3-ga tent bars (optional)
items.detail: Orange-tarp pojangmacha tents on the sidewalk: soju, grilled fish, gizzards. A yatai/yokocho night 10 min from bed.

food.name: Gaeseong Mandu Koong (Insadong)
food.note: Long-running Insadong house for North Korean-style dumplings and mandu-guk. Walk-in; confirm it is open on the day.

food.name: Gwangjang Market crawl: Soonhee-ne bindaetteok + Buchon Yukhoe
food.note: Share a bindaetteok, a yukhoe plate and a bottle of makgeolli; Buchon Yukhoe queues on Sunday evenings.

food.name: Jongno 3-ga pojangmacha
food.note: Some tents take Sunday off; pick a busy one.

rainy_swap: Huwon tours run in light rain (bring umbrellas). If it pours, skip the garden for Leeum Museum (open Sunday, closed Monday) or the National Museum of Korea; Mulbit is weather-dependent, so swap it for SPAREX Dongdaemun jjimjilbang.

title: Hanbok at the main palace, sunset on the city wall
summary: Monday is Gyeongbokgung's day (it closes Tuesday): wear hanbok for free entry and the guard ceremony, lunch in Seochon, then the short, steep Inwangsan fortress-wall hike for sunset over the palace and Bugaksan. Finish in Euljiro's retro back-alley bars.
autumn_note: Clear October air makes the Inwangsan view sharp; ginkgos around Gyeongbokgung are starting to yellow. Sunset ~17:53.

items.title: Hanbok rental near Gyeongbokgung
items.detail: Pick a shop by Gyeongbokgung station (exit 4/5) or Anguk. Basic 4-hour rental; hair styling extra.
items.booking: Walk-in, or book on Creatrip/Klook for a small discount.
items.tip: Return times are strict; ask for warm inner layers.

items.title: Gyeongbokgung Palace in hanbok
items.detail: Free in hanbok. See the 10:00 royal guard change at Gwanghwamun, Gyeonghoeru pavilion on its pond and Hyangwonjeong at the back. Geunjeongjeon's courtyard is partly fenced for works until Oct 31, but the throne hall is still visible.

items.title: Return hanbok, lunch in Seochon
items.detail: Tosokchon's ginseng chicken soup is a 5-minute walk west of the palace.

items.title: Seochon lanes, galleries and a cafe break
items.detail: Wander the hanok alleys west of the palace (Nuha-dong, Ogin-dong), small galleries and bookshops; rest over coffee before the climb.
items.tip: Many Tongin Market stalls and the dosirak cafe close on Mondays; don't plan lunch around them.

items.title: Inwangsan fortress-wall sunset hike
items.detail: From Sajik Park follow the 600-year-old city wall up the granite ridge to the 338 m summit (about 50-60 min, many stairs). Watch the sun go down behind you as Gyeongbokgung, Bugaksan and Namsan light up; descend the lit stairs.
items.tip: Bring a headlamp/phone light and water; sneakers with grip.

items.title: BBQ dinner, then Euljiro 'Hipjiro' bars
items.detail: Taxi to Geumdwaeji for charcoal-grilled pork, then 3 subway stops to Euljiro 3-ga: Nogari Alley's plastic tables, draft beer and hidden 3rd-floor bars among the print shops. Monday is a good night here (some places shut Sunday).

food.name: Tosokchon Samgyetang
food.note: Whole young chicken stuffed with sticky rice and ginseng. Fast-moving queue. Splurge alternative: Onjium (Joseon court cuisine above the palace wall, ~200k, CatchTable, hard to get).

food.name: Geumdwaeji Sikdang
food.note: Cult samgyeopsal and bone-in pork over briquettes, Seoul's Korean-BBQ benchmark. Daily 11:30-23:00; walk-in queue, so register and wait.

food.name: Euljiro Nogari Alley
food.note: Draft beer ~5,000 and dried pollock sticks ~2,500.

rainy_swap: Gyeongbokgung works under umbrellas (skip the hanbok). Replace Inwangsan with the National Museum of Korea (open Mondays, free), then Euljiro as planned.

title: To the Silla capital: tombs, stone tower, pond of lights
summary: A mid-morning KTX to Gyeongju, bags dropped in Bomun, then the flat, walkable heritage core: grassy royal tombs, Cheomseongdae, the Gyerim grove, Gyochon and Woljeonggyo, ending at Donggung & Wolji as its pavilions light up over the water.
autumn_note: Royal tomb mounds turn golden; Cheomseongdae's pink muhly is fading but silver grass and cosmos fill in. Foliage is early color only (Gyeongju peaks ~early Nov). Sunset ~17:47.

items.title: Taxi to Seoul Station
items.detail: About 15 min from Jongno with bags (~10k per car).

items.title: KTX Seoul → Gyeongju
items.detail: KTX-Sancheon 23. Gyeongju Station is the old Singyeongju, 15 km from town.

items.title: Taxi to the Bomun hotel, drop bags, taxi to town
items.detail: Station → Bomun ~30 min (~30k per car), drop bags at the front desk, then ~15 min (~12k) back into the heritage core.

items.title: Lunch, Daereungwon tombs and Cheonmachong
items.detail: After a Korean set lunch, walk among 23 grassy Silla royal mounds; Cheonmachong is the one you can enter, with gold-crown and Heavenly Horse replicas.
items.cost_note: admission may now be free; check at the gate

items.title: Hwangridan-gil coffee and Hwangnam-ppang
items.detail: Hanok cafe street on the tombs' west edge; buy warm red-bean Hwangnam-ppang at the 1939 original shop (also tomorrow's Ragung breakfast).

items.title: Cheomseongdae → Gyerim → Gyochon & Woljeonggyo
items.detail: The 2 km heritage walk: East Asia's oldest observatory in its flower fields, the ancient zelkova grove of Gyerim, the Choi family hanok village and the reconstructed covered bridge over Namcheon (cross the stepping stones for the classic photo).

items.title: Donggung Palace & Wolji Pond at dusk
items.detail: Arrive before sunset and stay as the pavilions light up and double in the still pond, Gyeongju's signature night view. A Tuesday visit dodges the weekend ticket queue.

items.title: Ssambap dinner, taxi to Bomun
items.detail: Short taxi to Ssambap Street south of Daereungwon for Gyeongju's lettuce-wrap feast, then ~15 min taxi back to the hotel.

food.name: Dosol Maeul
food.note: Great-value Korean set meal in a house near Daereungwon; queue at lunch.

food.name: Hwangnam Bread (main shop)
food.note: Gyeongju's omiyage since 1939, like Kamakura's hato sable. Box of 20 ~20,000.

food.name: Ssambap Street (Daereungwon south)
food.note: Dozens of side dishes, grilled pork and a mountain of leaves to wrap.

rainy_swap: Keep Cheonmachong (indoors) and move the Gyeongju National Museum (free) to today; Wolji is lovely in light rain with reflections on wet stone. Hwangridan-gil cafes for the gaps.

title: Bulguksa, the stone Buddha, and a private hot-spring night
summary: Korea's most famous temple and the Seokguram grotto in the morning, a court-style hanok lunch and the Silla gold crowns at the museum, then a short hop to Ragung: a hanok suite with its own outdoor hot-spring bath in a walled courtyard. This is the trip's Izu-ryokan night.
autumn_note: Bulguksa's maples around the entrance pond and the stone bridges are turning (forecast peak Oct 22-29, likely late in 2026, so expect partial color). A cool evening makes the open-air bath perfect.

items.title: Check out, taxi to Bulguksa
items.detail: Leave bags at the front desk; Bomun → Bulguksa ~15 min (~13k per car).

items.title: Bulguksa Temple
items.detail: UNESCO 8th-century temple: the Cheongungyo/Baegungyo stone stairway-bridges and the Dabotap and Seokgatap pagodas. Free entry since 2023.
items.tip: Sources disagree on opening (VisitKorea 2026: 09:00; older info: ~07:00). If it opens earlier, go earlier: school-trip buses arrive from ~10:00 on weekdays.

items.title: Seokguram Grotto
items.detail: Bus 12 (1,500 KRW, ~20 min, about hourly) or a taxi (~10k per car) up the Tohamsan ridge, then a 600 m forest walk to the granite Buddha gazing toward the East Sea.
items.tip: No photos inside. Hikers can instead walk up the old 3.2 km trail from Bulguksa (~1 h).

items.title: Hanok course lunch at Yoseokgung
items.detail: Taxi ~30 min down to Gyochon (~25k per car) for the closest thing in town to a kaiseki meal: many small seasonal dishes in the Choi family's old hanok compound.
items.booking: Reserve by phone or Naver (ask the hotel to call); lunch course ~50-70k.

items.title: Gyeongju National Museum
items.detail: Korea's best Silla collection: the gold crowns, Wolji pond finds and the 19-ton Emille Bell in the garden. Free.

items.title: Collect bags, check in to Ragung
items.detail: Taxi via the first hotel to pick up bags (~20 min in total within Bomun), then check in at Ragung by Silla Millennium Park.

items.title: Private outdoor hot-spring bath
items.detail: Your own stone tub of soft hot-spring water in a walled hanok courtyard, warm ondol floors inside. Soak at dusk, again after dinner, and at dawn.
items.tip: No breakfast or dinner is served; drip coffee is in the room. Taxis are scarce at night, so book Kakao T rides both ways.

items.title: Hanu beef dinner in Bomun
items.detail: 5-minute taxi to Gyeongju Cheonnyeon Hanu, the livestock co-op's butcher-restaurant: pick Gyeongju hanu at the counter and grill it at the table. Back to the bath by 20:15.

food.name: Yoseokgung
food.note: Hanjeongsik course in a historic hanok by Woljeonggyo; book ahead.

food.name: Gyeongju Cheonnyeon Hanu (Bomun)
food.note: Butcher-counter hanu (meat by weight + ~6,000 table charge); yukhoe bibimbap 13,000 and hanu soup 13,000 for lighter eaters. 545-9 Bomun-ro, 054-741-8006; hours not verified, so call or have Ragung call. Coordinates approximate.

rainy_swap: Bulguksa and Seokguram are fine in drizzle (Seokguram is under cover). In heavy rain, drop Seokguram, do the museum longer, and get to Ragung early: a hot-spring bath in the rain is still the point.

title: Seaside temple and the little coastal capsule
summary: A last dawn soak, a train that drops you on Busan's Haeundae side, an omakase lunch, then the Kamakura day: Haedong Yonggungsa on its sea rocks and the pastel Sky Capsule creeping along the old coastal railway into the sunset. Weekday timing keeps both bearable.
autumn_note: Busan stays green in October; the draw is clear, dry sea air and golden late-afternoon light. Sunset ~17:45.

items.title: Dawn bath, slow morning at Ragung
items.detail: One more private soak with drip coffee and yesterday's Hwangnam-ppang.

items.title: Taxi to Gyeongju Station
items.detail: ~30 min (~28k per car). Book the Kakao T car the night before.

items.title: ITX-Maeum Gyeongju → Sinhaeundae
items.detail: Donghae-line train straight to the Haeundae side of Busan.

items.title: Drop bags, omakase lunch in Haeundae
items.detail: Taxi to the hotel to drop bags (Paradise is 5 min; Aqua Palace in Gwangalli ~15 min, then back), then a sushi counter lunch at Iwa near Haeundae Beach.
items.booking: Iwa: phone +82 10-8543-3356 (open daily 11:30-22:00); ask your hotel to call. Book now.

items.title: Haedong Yonggungsa seaside temple
items.detail: Taxi ~20 min (~15k per car). Down the 108 steps to a temple built on the surf-battered rocks, with a sea-facing Guanyin statue: the Kamakura-Hasedera feeling, on the water.
items.tip: Weekday afternoons are far calmer than weekends.

items.title: Cheongsapo twin lighthouses and Daritdol Skywalk
items.detail: Taxi ~15 min to the little fishing harbor, then walk out on the glass-floored skywalk over the rocks.

items.title: Sky Capsule Cheongsapo → Mipo at golden hour
items.detail: A private pastel pod for the three of you, crawling 7-10 m above the sea on the old Donghae Nambu line toward the Haeundae skyline as the light turns gold. The Enoden-in-Kamakura moment.
items.booking: Klook/KKday (easiest) or bluelinepark.com; book a 16:30-17:00 Cheongsapo departure now.

items.title: Haeundae Beach sunset, then hot spring
items.detail: Walk the beach from Mipo at sunset. Sweet/splurge tiers: unlimited Cimer sea-view hot spring and outdoor ocean pool at Paradise tonight. Value tier: Spa Land Centum (26k, to 22:00, last entry 21:00) or an early night in Gwangalli.
items.cost_note: Cimer included in the Paradise Special Deal; Spa Land 26,000 not in budget

food.name: Iwa (sushi omakase)
food.note: Michelin-listed counter whose chef patented his own fish-aging method; best-value omakase in Busan. Daily 11:30-22:00. Book by phone +82 10-8543-3356 (ask your hotel to call). CatchTable alternative: Sushi Nee at L7 Haeundae (lunch 60k).

food.name: Geumsu Bokguk (Haeundae flagship)
food.note: Clean, delicate pufferfish soup, a light dinner after the omakase lunch. Open 24 h, walk-in.

food.name: Haeundae Traditional Market
food.note: Sangguk-ine tteokbokki and eomuk if anyone is still hungry.

rainy_swap: The capsule and Beach Train run in normal rain; in a storm swap them for Spa Land Centum and BUSAN X the SKY observatory, keeping Haedong Yonggungsa if the sea is safe.

title: Old harbor Busan: painted hills, fish market, white cliffs
summary: Move to the Gwangalli hotel, then west Busan: Gamcheon's pastel hillside early, lunch upstairs at Jagalchi on live-picked hoe, and Huinnyeoul's white cliff village for sunset over the anchored ships. Dinner back east: Haeundae's legendary beef galbi, or the Mori kaiseki splurge.
autumn_note: Jeon-eo (gizzard shad) and galchi are autumn favorites at Jagalchi. Sunset ~17:46.

items.title: Move bags to Gwangalli-Planet16
items.detail: Value tier: walk ~200 m from Aqua Palace. Sweet/splurge: taxi ~15 min from Paradise (an early Cimer soak first). Leave bags at Planet16 until check-in.

items.title: Gamcheon Culture Village
items.detail: Taxi ~35 min (~25k per car) to the top and walk down through the pastel refugee-era houses, art installations and the Little Prince lookout before the tour groups.

items.title: Jagalchi Fish Market: pick it, eat it upstairs
items.detail: Taxi ~15 min. Choose live fish on the ground floor, have it sliced and eat on 2F with a view of the harbor; finish with a spicy maeuntang from the bones.
items.tip: Agree the price per kg and weight before the knife goes in.

items.title: BIFF Square and Gukje Market
items.detail: Seed-stuffed ssiat hotteok from the BIFF stalls, then the postwar Gukje Market alleys. Coffee break nearby.

items.title: Huinnyeoul village and Jeollyeong coastal walk
items.detail: Taxi ~15 min to Yeongdo, stop at Samjin Eomuk's flagship, then walk the white cliffside lanes and the seaside path below, ending at a cliff cafe for sunset over dozens of anchored ships.
items.tip: Have legs left? Swap Gukje Market for Taejongdae's cliff loop (Danubi road train ~4,000).

items.title: Dinner in Haeundae, back to Gwangalli
items.detail: Taxi ~35 min to Haeundae Amso Galbi (or Mori for a 19:00 kaiseki seating), then 15 min to Gwangalli to check in and see Gwangan Bridge lit up.

food.name: Jagalchi Market hoe (2F restaurants)
food.note: Platter for 3 ~60-120k plus ~5,000 pp table fee. The freshest raw fish of the trip.

food.name: Samjin Eomuk (Yeongdo flagship)
food.note: Busan's fish-cake institution since 1953; try the croquette-style eomuk.

food.name: Haeundae Amso Galbi (or Mori kaiseki)
food.note: Decades-old marinated cow-beef galbi; queues, so add your name and walk the beach. Splurge: Mori, Japanese-style kaiseki with Busan seafood (~250k pp, Fri seating 19:00, closed Mon; phone +82 51-731-9889 or CatchTable).

rainy_swap: Gukje Market and Jagalchi are covered; replace Gamcheon and Huinnyeoul with Spa Land Centum or the Busan Museum of Modern History, then dinner as planned.

title: Cliff walk, Dongnae hot spring, drones over the bridge
summary: The Igidae cliff boardwalk in the cool morning, an afternoon soak in Asia's largest hot-spring bathhouse, then a raw-fish dinner facing Gwangan Bridge and the Saturday drone show from the beach outside your hotel.
autumn_note: October is the best month for Igidae; silver grass on the Oryukdo headland. Drone show theme Oct 24: 'Forest's Melody'.

items.title: Oryukdo Skywalk
items.detail: Taxi ~20 min (~12k per car) to the glass horseshoe over the cliffs where the East Sea meets the South Sea.

items.title: Igidae coastal walk (Galmaet-gil 2)
items.detail: About 4.7 km of cliffside boardwalks, suspension bridges and coves heading north, with Gwangan Bridge and the Haeundae skyline ahead the whole way.
items.tip: Many stairs; proper shoes. Sections close after storms.

items.title: Pork gukbap lunch
items.detail: Short taxi to Daeyeon for Busan's signature milky pork-bone soup.

items.title: Hurshimchung hot spring (Dongnae)
items.detail: Metro or taxi (~30 min) to Oncheonjang: about 40 baths under a glass dome fed by the 1,300-year-old Dongnae spring, including open-air and cypress tubs. Reopened May 2026 after renovation.
items.tip: Bathing is nude and gender-separated; tattoos are generally tolerated.

items.title: Millak hoe facing Gwangan Bridge
items.detail: Buy fish on 1F of the Millak fishermen's market and eat upstairs as the bridge lights come on.

items.title: Gwangalli M Drone Light Show
items.detail: About 1,100 drones over the bridge for ~12 minutes at 19:00 and again at 21:00. Watch the first from the sand in front of the hotel, then a beach bar, and catch the quieter 21:00 show.
items.tip: Arrive 30 min early for a central spot. Cancelled for wind or rain with little notice.

food.name: Ssangdungi Dwaeji Gukbap
food.note: The Busan comfort-food classic; queue moves fast.

food.name: Millak Fishermen's Live Fish Market
food.note: Flatfish ~30k/kg, setting fee ~6,000 pp; ask for a window table. Go by 17:30: the drone show fills every seat.

rainy_swap: Skip Igidae; spend longer at Hurshimchung or Spa Land Centum. If the drone show is cancelled, watch the bridge lights from a Gwangalli bar instead.

title: Slow beach morning, KTX north, fly home
summary: A lazy Gwangalli morning, milmyeon by Busan Station, then the KTX to Seoul and the AREX straight to the airport with time to spare.

items.title: Gwangalli beach morning
items.detail: Coffee and a beach walk; Millak Waterfront Park at the north end for one last bridge view.

items.title: Check out, taxi to Busan Station
items.detail: ~30 min (~20k per car).

items.title: Milmyeon lunch by the station
items.detail: Choryang's wartime-refugee cold wheat noodles, a 5-minute walk from Busan Station.

items.title: KTX Busan → Seoul
items.detail: KTX-Sancheon 38.
items.booking: Korail+ / korail.com, book now (Sunday northbound sells out).

items.title: AREX Express to Incheon T1
items.detail: Non-stop 43 min. At the airport ~17:00 for the 21:55 flight; eat and shop airside.

items.title: Air Premia departs ICN
items.detail: Confirm the terminal (T1 assumed) the day before.

food.name: Gwangalli beachfront cafe
food.note: Any bridge-view cafe on Gwanganhaebyeon-ro.

food.name: Choryang Milmyeon
food.note: Busan-only cold noodles; mul (broth) or bibim (spicy).

rainy_swap: Nothing changes; spend the morning at a cafe or Spa Land Centum (lockers for bags) before the train.
